ordinary_statute_amendments.title_he: חוק גמלאות לנושאי משרה ברשויות השלטון, תשכ"ט-1969
amends: Basic Law: The President of the State
ordinary_statute_amendments.note: Section 6(a) amended Basic Law: The President of the State (section 16, salary and payments). Listed by Wikisource in the President page header, by Nevo (via the WIPO Lex copy of its consolidated text) as "תיקון מס' 1 בסעיף 6(א) לחוק גמלאות...", and by the Knesset database as an indirect amendment with CorrectionNumber 1; this is why the first Basic-Law-titled amendment is "תיקון מס' 2" and why Hebrew Wikipedia counts ten amendments. Not counted as an entry.

Listed by Wikisource beside the 1968 Basic Law and bound by the Knesset database to it as a "direct amendment" ("מתקן, ישיר"), but its text contains only a transitional provision (the serving government is deemed to serve under the Basic Law), amendments to other statutes and repeals; it does not amend the text of the Basic Law. Nevo's table for the 1968 law omits it. Recorded here for completeness, not counted.

discrepancies: Wikisource lists ס"ח תשנ"ה 42 (חוק-יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס' 8), 1994) under the 1992 version as well as the 1968 version; Nevo's table for the 1992 law (archived 2021) and the Knesset database bind it only to the 1968 law, and its published text amends only sections 5(ב1) and 34(ב) of the 1968 law. Counts: Wikisource 11 amending items for the 1992 law, Nevo 10, Knesset database 10, Hebrew Wikipedia "תוקן 10 פעמים".
חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 12) (1991): Wikisource gives ס"ח תשנ"א עמ' 90, Nevo עמ' 91 (the Government section); Knesset database: publication page 90, binding page 91.
חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 42 והוראת שעה) (2015): Wikisource Government page gives ס"ח תשע"ה עמ' 249, Wikisource Knesset page and Knesset database 248 (binding page 249).
חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 49) (2020): Wikisource עמ' 70; Knesset database publication page 70, binding page 72 (the Government section).

Basic Law: The President numbering: the published titles "תיקון מס' 5" (1998) and "תיקון מס' 6" (2001) are the fourth and fifth amendments (Wikisource flags "[צ"ל 4]" and "[צ"ל: 5]"; Nevo and the Knesset database number them 4 and 5), and two different laws are titled "תיקון מס' 6" (2001 and 2003). Nevo and the Knesset database count the 1969 pensions statute as amendment no. 1.
חוק-יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל (תיקון מס' 3): the gazette footnote gives passage on כ"ז בתשרי התשפ"ה (29.10.2024); Hebrew Wikipedia says 28.10.2024.
חוק-יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס' 2) (1979): the footnote's Hebrew date ט"ז בחשון תש"ם converts to 6.11.1979 (Nevo: commencement 6.11.1979); the OCR of the archived scan reads the Gregorian day as 8.

חוק הממשלה (הוראות מעבר), תשכ"ח-1968: Wikisource lists it with the 1968 Basic Law and the Knesset database records it as a direct amendment; Nevo's table omits it and its text does not amend the Basic Law (see ordinary_statute_amendments).

Nevo's open page for the 2001 Government law is headed "נוסח עדכני נכון ליום: 22-07-2026", later than the last amendment found in any source (תיקון מס' 13, May 2025); whether a 2026 amendment exists could not be verified because Nevo's amendments table is behind a login; Wikisource (last revised 30.3.2026), the Knesset database mirror (latest publication 13.5.2025) and web searches show none.

Wikisource labels as "תיקון: תשל"ו" in section 2 of Basic Law: The Army refer to a corrigendum (ת"ט, ס"ח תשל"ו 241), not an amending law; the Knesset database records it as "תיקון טעות". Other corrigenda noted by Wikisource (Government 1968 ס"ח תשכ"ח XII; Government 1992 ס"ח תשנ"ו 386; President ס"ח תשכ"ד XII and תשנ"ו 387) are likewise not entries.
deviations: Hebrew Wikisource has no separate pages for the repealed 1968 and 1992 versions of Basic Law: The Government (checked by prefix, title and full-text searches of the Wikisource API); their amendment lists were taken from the "חוק קודם" blocks in the header of the current page https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק-יסוד:_הממשלה, which lists both earlier laws and every amending law with its ס"ח reference.

Nevo: the law pages with the amendments table (nevo.co.il/law/...) require a one-time-code login and were not used; the open "law_html/law00" pages give only the consolidated text and a currency date. Nevo cross-checks therefore rest on (a) Wayback Machine captures of Nevo's pages for the two repealed versions (btl0630.htm, 2022; btl0631.htm, 2021), which carry full tables, (b) WIPO Lex reproductions of Nevo's consolidated texts (Government 2001 as of 2016, President as of 2014) and (c) the currency dates on the open pages (Jerusalem 30.10.2024; President, Army, Israel Lands, State Comptroller 18.9.2023). For Jerusalem, State Comptroller, Israel Lands and Army no Nevo amendments table was available.

An additional official source was used in place of the blocked Knesset sites: the Knesset national legislation database tables (KNS_IsraelLaw, KNS_LawBinding, KNS_Bill, KNS_DocumentBill) mirrored at production.oknesset.org, which give published titles, publication dates, booklet and page numbers, direct/indirect classification, amendment numbers and temporary-legislation flags for every law bound to the eight law records (Government 1968 = 2000038, 1992 = 2000039, 2001 = 2000040, Israel Lands 2000048, President 2000050, Army 2000041, Jerusalem 2000045, State Comptroller 2000047).

Passage dates: all but one come from the "נתקבל/התקבל בכנסת ביום" footnotes of the Knesset gazette PDFs fetched through web.archive.org (fs.knesset.gov.il itself and the Knesset database site redirect to a geo-block page), text-extracted locally; each Hebrew date was converted with the macOS Hebrew calendar to check the OCR of the Gregorian date. Jerusalem 1980 uses Wikisource's signature block because the archived scan's footnote was not machine-readable.

Kind values: three laws whose titles contain הוראת שעה are labelled "amendment and temporary provision" rather than one of the four listed values; no Basic-Law-titled law in this set is a free-standing temporary provision.

A law amending more than one of the six Basic Laws is one entry placed under its principal subject (the Basic Law named in its title); Basic Law: The Knesset amendments nos. 12, 41, 42 and 49 are therefore entries with principal_subject Basic Law: The Knesset, and the 1968-series "תיקון מס' 9" (1996) is one entry listing both the 1968 and 1992 versions.

Hebrew Wikipedia was used only for counts and cross-checks (1968 law: 9 amendments; 1992 law: 10; President: 10 including the 1969 statute and Knesset no. 41; Jerusalem: 3; State Comptroller: 2; Army and Israel Lands: none), all consistent with the entries except as noted in discrepancies.
About 55 tool calls were used; no file in the repository folder was read or written; scratch files were kept in a fresh subfolder of the scratch directory.
